citation.title: Chapter 7: Diagnostics
citation.authors: Donné A.J.H., Costley A.E., Barnsley R., et al. and the ITPA Topical Group on Diagnostics
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1088/0029-5515/47/6/S07 (this paper's DOI, from the p.2 header)

scope_read.pdf_pages: 1–49 (p.1 is a download cover; article pp.2–49)
scope_read.limitations: Table 7 assigns status by colour, and the extracted text loses the colour key, so the assessed status of each row cannot be read. ITER design and requirements review only; no estimator, dataset or KSTAR content.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Edge ion temperature requirement: 100 ms, 10%, with a defined spatial range.
claim_checks.source_finding: Row 28 sets edge Ti at r/a>0.9: range 0.05–10 keV, 100 ms time resolution, 10% accuracy, spatial resolution TBD. Core Ti at r/a<0.9: 0.5–40 keV, 100 ms, a/10, 10%.
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: ITER diagnostic specifications list edge ion temperature (r/a>0.9) at 100 ms time resolution and 10% accuracy, with spatial resolution still to be determined [Donné 2007].
claim_checks.qualification: These are ITER targets, not KSTAR requirements and not achieved performance. The edge spatial resolution is TBD, so no number should be cited for it. Do not equate a pedestal-top chord with r/a>0.9 unless this is shown separately.

claim_checks.source_finding: Table 1 lists core Ti as a control measurement from the D/T phase onward, and core Ti(r) for evaluation. Steady-state control adds high-resolution Te/Ti gradient measurements. The text suggests ITB control may work better on Te/Ti/rotation gradients than on q. Edge Ti is not given an explicit control role.
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: ITER planning treats core ion temperature and, for advanced scenarios, ion-temperature gradients as candidate control quantities, for example for transport-barrier control [Donné 2007].
claim_checks.qualification: Gradient control is stated as plausible ('may be more successful'), not demonstrated. Do not attribute an edge-Ti control role to this source.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Carbon charge-exchange spectroscopy is a planned basis for Ti.
claim_checks.source_finding: The authors state that ITER Ti will rely on the C VI charge-exchange spectrum. They expect S/N above 30 near the axis, extrapolated from JET data. Passive x-ray crystal spectroscopy is presented as a complementary Ti method.
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Charge-exchange spectroscopy on intrinsic carbon is a planned primary route to ion temperature on ITER [Donné 2007].
claim_checks.qualification: The S/N figure is a projection, not a measurement. CES-derived Ti remains a reported diagnostic quantity, not independent truth.

input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: The paper discusses consistency cross-checks (Fig.9, p.17) and possible ECE/Thomson disagreement under distorted distributions (p.15). It does not treat any diagnostic as ground truth.

validation.unknowns: How the Table 2 numbers were derived is only referenced, to [7] and [11].

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Nothing. These are specifications and design status.
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Any latency or real-time Ti delivery. The 100 ms figure is a resolution target, not a computation budget.

forbidden_inferences: that the ITER 100 ms/10% targets apply to KSTAR or to our chord
that our 10 ms grid 'meets' or 'exceeds' an ITER requirement
that edge Ti is specified as a control input
that the Te justification in Table 3 (10 ms) applies to Ti
that the ITER CXRS performance is demonstrated
that CES labels are physical truth
that the edge spatial resolution is specified
competing_or_complementary: Complementary motivation. It provides context for why Ti and its gradients matter and how often they are needed. It neither proposes nor evaluates nowcasting.
followup_sources_if_material: ITER Physics Expert Group on Diagnostics 1999 Nucl. Fusion 39 2541 (ref [7], origin of the requirements)
von Hellermann M. et al 2004 Rev. Sci. Instrum. 75 3458 (ref [98], ITER CXRS performance); the DOIs of these cited papers are not given in this PDF
